explain.say: On 14 October 1962 an American U-2 spy plane photographed something new in the fields of western Cuba: launch sites for Soviet nuclear missiles that could reach most US cities within minutes. For thirteen days the world stood nearer to nuclear war than ever before or since. Look at the timeline.

explain.say: Why did Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev take this gamble? Look at the sizes, estimates for 1962: the United States had about 25,500 nuclear warheads, the Soviet Union about 3,300, and US missiles stood in Turkey, right by Soviet borders. A failed US-backed invasion of Cuba in 1961 made Fidel Castro want protection. Which reason would worry you most if you were Khrushchev?

items.label: US warheads
items.ask: Why did Khrushchev put missiles in Cuba?

explain.say: Now the map. Cuba lies only about 150 kilometres from Florida. Kennedy's advisers argued for air strikes or invasion. Instead, on 22 October, he announced a quarantine, a naval blockade by another name, since a blockade is an act of war. Soviet ships approached, then turned back. Why choose a word like quarantine?

Watch how it ended. Robert Kennedy met the Soviet ambassador secretly; Khrushchev sent two letters, the second also asking for US missiles to leave Turkey. On 28 October the deal: Soviet missiles out of Cuba, a US promise not to invade, and, kept secret for years, US missiles out of Turkey. Who do you think gave more?

explain.say: On Black Saturday, 27 October, a U-2 was shot down, and on a Soviet submarine the officer Vasili Arkhipov refused to approve firing a nuclear torpedo. Afterwards came a hotline and a test ban in 1963. Great work. Exam tip: once the secret Turkey deal was known, historians saw compromise, not simple victory.

faq.q: What was the Cuban Missile Crisis?
faq.a: A thirteen-day confrontation in October 1962 after the United States discovered Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba. It brought the superpowers close to nuclear war and ended when Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles.
asks: When was the Cuban Missile Crisis?

faq.q: Why did Khrushchev put missiles in Cuba?
faq.a: To defend Cuba after the US-backed Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961, to narrow the huge US lead in nuclear weapons, to answer US missiles in Turkey and perhaps to gain leverage over Berlin.
asks: What was the Bay of Pigs?

faq.q: How was the Cuban Missile Crisis resolved?
faq.a: Through a naval quarantine, back-channel talks between Robert Kennedy and Soviet ambassador Anatoly Dobrynin, and a deal on 28 October 1962: Soviet missiles left Cuba, the USA pledged not to invade, and US Jupiter missiles were secretly removed from Turkey.
asks: Did the USA remove missiles from Turkey?

faq.q: Why was it called a quarantine?
faq.a: Under international law a blockade is an act of war, so the Kennedy administration called its naval interception of ships carrying weapons to Cuba a quarantine.

A Soviet naval officer aboard submarine B-59 on 27 October 1962. When US ships dropped practice depth charges to force it to surface, he refused to agree to launch a nuclear-armed torpedo, which needed the consent of three senior officers.

facts: A U-2 photographed Soviet missile sites in Cuba on 14 October 1962.
Khrushchev announced the missiles' withdrawal on 28 October 1962.
The Partial Test Ban Treaty was signed in August 1963.

quiz.say: In 1962 the USA had about 25,500 warheads and the USSR about 3,300. Roughly how many times more did the USA have?
quiz.why: 25,500 divided by 3,300 is about 7.7, close to 8.

quiz.say: What was the secret part of the deal that ended the crisis?
quiz.show: Kept secret for years was that…
quiz.why: Kennedy quietly agreed to remove Jupiter missiles from Turkey, which happened in 1963.

wrong.1: Castro stayed in power for decades.
